newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.S. first to take Iraq oil from Gulf - minister. [CORRECTED 13:42 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. first to take Iraq oil from Gulf - minister. [CORRECTED 13:42 GMT]

text.p: Iraq's Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said two U.S. firms were the first to load Iraqi crude from Mina al-Bakr terminal on Sunday.

"The first oil quantities exported via Mina al-Bakr were part of deals struck with U.S. firms Coastal Petroleum and Bay Oil (corrects from "Day Oil")," Rasheed said in remarks carried by the official Iraqi News Agency (INA)
Rasheed said platforms at Mina al-Bakr, Iraq's southern export outlet, and its annexes were in a proper working condition.

"At present we are loading 500,000 barrels of oil into the Star of Africa anchoring currently at the port. It is hoped the tanker will be filled with two million barrels. The ship will leave within the coming 48 hours," Rasheed said.

He said Iraq's proven reserves of 112 billion barrels of oil "could rise to 214 billion and simple mathematics mean oil will be sufficient for Iraq for more than 100 years to come, even if it exported three million barrels per day," Rasheed said.
Rasheed was in Basra supervising government celebrations to mark the start of exports from Gulf terminals for the first time since sanctions were imposed on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Vice-President Taha Yassin Ramadan pressed the button to unleash Iraqi partial exports via Mina al-Bakr terminal, INA reported.

"President Saddam Hussein had delegated Vice-President Taha Yassin Ramadan to attend the ceremonies (in Basra) where he pressed the operating button of the pumping station at Northern Rumeila oilfeild," INA said.
